articles.title: ReNew Secures USD 100 Million from FMO in Dutch Development Bank’s Largest-Ever Single-Ticket Investment in India’s Energy Sector

articles.summary: 10-year financing to support ReNew’s under-construction renewable energy portfolio and deepen access to long-term international capital Gurugram, India; October 13, 2026: ReNew (“ ReNew ” or “the Company”), one of India’s leading decarbonisation solutions companies, today announced that it has secured a USD 100 million (approximately INR 955 crore) financing facility from FMO (Nederlandse Financierings -Maatschappij voor Ontwikkelingslanden N.V.), the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Extended to ReNew Solar Power Private Limited under the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR), the 10-year financing will support renewable energy projects currently under construction across the ReNew group. The transaction marks FMO’s largest single-ticket investment in India’s energy sector and its largest 2X-aligned corporate financing in Asia to date, underscoring the growing role of international development finance in supporting India’s clean energy transition. The facility qualifies under the 2X Challenge, a global initiative focused on advancing women’s economic participation and empowerment through investment. Proceeds from the INR-denominated financing will be deployed towards ReNew’s under-construction renewable energy projects. The long-term financing strengthens ReNew’s access to international capital and further diversifies its funding base across domestic and global markets. With a 10-year tenor aligned with the long operating life of renewable energy assets, the facility provides stable capital to support the Company’s expanding portfolio and continued growth. Kailash Vaswani, Chief Financial Officer, ReNew , said: “This financing is a strong endorsement of ReNew’s scale, execution capabilities and long-term growth strategy, and reflects the confidence of leading global institutions in India’s clean energy opportunity. The 10-year facility gives us access to stable, long-term capital at a critical stage of our portfolio build-out, while further diversifying our funding sources across international and domestic markets. We are delighted to strengthen our partnership with FMO and channel this capital towards projects that will contribute to India’s rapidly expanding clean energy ecosystem.” Marnix Monsfort , Director & Head – Energy, FMO, said: “We are pleased to partner with ReNew on this 2X-aligned investment and support the Company’s growth ambitions. As FMO’s largest investment in India’s energy sector, this transaction demonstrates our commitment to supporting India’s energy transition through impactful, large-scale financing solutions. ReNew has established itself as a leading renewable energy company in the country, and we look forward to supporting its continued contribution to India’s clean energy future.” The financing comes at a pivotal moment in India’s energy transition, as the country accelerates the deployment of renewable energy and the investment required to build the infrastructure of a low-carbon economy. For ReNew , the transaction reinforces its ability to mobilise long-term global capital at scale and deploy it towards projects that expand India’s clean energy capacity. It also deepens the Company’s relationship with FMO and reflects a shared commitment to financing an energy transition that is sustainable, inclusive and economically resilient. About ReNew ReNew is a leading decarbonization solutions company listed on Nasdaq (Nasdaq: RNW, RNWWW). ReNew’s clean energy portfolio of 20.5 GW (including 1.7 GW/6.2 GWh of BESS) on a gross basis as of August 18, 2026, is one of the largest globally. In addition to being a major independent power producer in India, we provide end-to-end solutions in a just and inclusive manner in the areas of clean energy, value-added energy offerings through digitalization, storage, and carbon markets that are increasingly integral to addressing climate change. In addition, ReNew has 6.4 GW of solar module and 2.5 GW of solar cell manufacturing capacities and is expanding its solar cells manufacturing capacity by another 4 GW, which is expected to be operational by December 2026. For more information, visit www.renew.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, X, and Instagram. Media enquiries: pr@renew.com About FMO FMO is the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. As a leading impact investor, FMO supports sustainable private sector growth in developing countries and emerging markets by investing in ambitious projects and entrepreneurs. FMO believes that a strong private sector leads to economic and social development and has a 50+ year proven track-record in empowering entrepreneurs to make local economies more inclusive, productive, resilient and sustainable. FMO focuses on three sectors that have high development impact: Agribusiness, Food & Water, Energy, and Financial Institutions. With a total committed portfolio of EUR ~13 billion spanning over 85 countries, FMO is one of the larger bilateral private sector development banks globally. articles.summary: Source: BBC News | Category: Interviews | Date: 16th Sep 2026 ReNew Founder, Chairman & CEO, Sumant Sinha , in conversation with Sally Bundock of the BBC News , highlighted India’s rising global presence and the BRICS summit’s dedication to collective progress. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has positioned India as a global voice for clean energy adoption and acceleration. Climate change remains the defining challenge, the very reason ReNew was founded. For India, geopolitics has sharpened the urgency: sovereignty demands a stronger domestic base. Sumant underscored that most of India’s incremental electricity demand growth now comes from renewables. Over the next 10–15 years, India will steadily reduce dependence on fossil fuels, building resilience and competitiveness through clean energy. Under PM Modi’s leadership, India is not just adapting, it is shaping the global energy transition.
